from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
out=Path('tmp/pdfs')
out.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA',r.metadata)
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
    text=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    (out/f'page-{i+1:02}.txt').write_text(text)
    print(f'PAGE {i+1}: {len(text)} chars; media box {p.mediabox}')
print((out/'page-01.txt').read_text())
PY"

from pathlib import Path
p=Path('tmp/pdfs')
files=list(p.glob('page-*.txt'))+list(p.glob('render-*.png'))
for f in files:
    f.unlink()
p.rmdir()
print(f'Removed {len(files)} temporary extraction and rendering files.')
PY"

strengths: MaskSub provides a simple, technically coherent way to incorporate heavy masking into supervised learning. Its shared-weight, stop-gradient distillation objective requires no additional inference computation or model parameters. The supported practical benefits provide a stronger case for acceptance despite moderate conceptual novelty.

The core improvements are consistent across strong training recipes and model sizes. Table 1 reports gains of 0.6–0.7 percentage points over DeiT-III at 400 epochs and 0.3–0.5 points at 800 epochs. Table A.12 strengthens this evidence with repeated runs: ViT-B improves from 83.46±0.04% to 84.08±0.02%.

The training-cost comparisons help establish that gains exceed those obtainable simply by training longer. In Table 7, ViT-B with MaskSub reaches 84.1% using 25 GPU-days, versus 83.7% using 26 GPU-days for the longer baseline. Table 8 also demonstrates a favorable accuracy–cost tradeoff against CoSub.

Evaluation is unusually broad for a training regularizer, covering MAE, BEiTv2 and CLIP fine-tuning, ResNet, Swin, transfer learning, and robustness. The supplement includes ADE20K segmentation and COCO detection, while Table A.4 reports substantial ImageNet-A improvements, including 51.9% to 58.3% for ViT-H.

Ablations examine the distillation loss, masking ratio, loss weights, and alternative drop regularizations. Algorithm 1 and Tables B.1–B.2 make the main implementation understandable, and the supplementary repeated-run results and linked code support reproducibility.
weaknesses: Originality lies mainly in combining established online self-distillation with masked-token dropping and validating the combination under strong recipes. The conceptual distinction from GradAug, CoSub, and related consistency methods is modest. Table A.7 also shows that the zero-masking variant already improves the baseline from 77.4% to 78.4%, so part of the benefit comes from the additional consistency objective.

The explanation of automatic difficulty control exceeds the evidence. Equation 3 applies distillation to every example; it does not restrict masking supervision to successfully classified images as Section 3.1 claims. An incorrect, confident teacher can also supply a strong target. Figure 3 supports changing gradient magnitudes during training, but does not establish the claimed relationship to example difficulty.

Some comparative conclusions are unsupported. Table 6 compares MaskSub using the strong RSB recipe against self-distillation methods using different, weaker recipes. These numbers cannot establish either superiority of the distillation mechanism or the asserted incompatibility of earlier methods with modern recipes. The controlled comparisons in Tables 8–9 are more persuasive.

The claimed general applicability needs qualification. In Table 10, adding MaskSub during fine-tuning reduces ViT-B CIFAR-100 accuracy from 91.9% to 89.6% with the same MaskSub-pretrained backbone. Section 4.2 also states that CLIP's best-checkpoint accuracy is unchanged. Moreover, ResNet and Swin require roughly twice the training computation because token dropping is unavailable.

Statistical support is uneven. Repeated runs substantiate important classification results, but uncertainty is not reported for the 0.1-point BEiTv2 gains or the 0.2-point COCO detection improvement. These smaller results provide weaker evidence for the repeated claim of significant improvements across settings.

There are correctable reporting errors: Section 4.4 claims one-sixth of GradAug's training cost, whereas Table 9 gives 8.6 versus 23.4 GPU-days, approximately 37% of the total cost. Table 10 labels the ViT-S Cars improvement from 80.9% to 92.2% as +1.3 rather than +11.3 points. These do not overturn the central results.
